signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew vs Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 156.22, holding below its daily SMA20 at 158.96 and SMA50 at 160.48. OIS SOFR at 3.66% against TONA at 0.98% maintains a +268bp carry differential favoring the dollar, reinforced by a policy rate gap of Fed 3.75% versus BoJ 1.0% providing +275bp. However, the options market exhibits an aggressive structural put skew, with the 1-month 25-delta Risk Reversal at -2.54 alongside elevated realized volatility where HV30 sits at 10.7% against an ATM IV of 7.2%, reflecting a -3.5% vol risk premium. While CFTC leveraged funds remain net short JPY by -111,297 contracts at the 2nd percentile of their 52-week range, fresh reports of South Korea considering military contributions in the Strait of Hormuz layer geopolitical tail risk onto existing carry exposures, elevating downside hedging demand despite low broader market volatility. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish USD/JPY, constrained by options downside skew against positive carry. Catalyst: Japan GDP release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Spot closes firmly above the SMA20 at 158.96, prompting systematic short-covering and neutralizing put demand.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7203, comfortably positioned above its SMA20 at 0.7135, SMA50 at 0.7041, and SMA200 at 0.6988. Institutional positioning shows leveraged funds net long AUD at +50,250 contracts, representing the 94th percentile and a z-score of +1.79 within its 52-week distribution, marking an overstretched posture even as weekly adds paused with a WoW contraction of -3,328 contracts. Concurrently, retail sentiment sits at an extreme 90% short, fading the multi-week institutional advance while BEER fair value model flags the pair as rich at z = +1.81σ against a modeled fair value of 0.7081. Although RBA cash rate at 4.35% versus Fed at 3.75% provides a -60bp carry advantage favoring AUD alongside a positive AONIA-SOFR spread of -69bp, stretched positioning and options 25d RR skewing mildly defensive at -0.47 limit immediate extension room. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD, late-trend positioning saturation capping immediate upside. Catalyst: Australia retail sentiment release at 08:00 UTC. Risk: Leveraged funds expand net longs past the +60,000 threshold on strong commodity traction, extending the trend.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Macro Divergence + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1613, wedged between its 20-day SMA at 1.1611 and 200-day SMA at 1.1638. OIS pricing reflects a wide gap with SOFR at 3.66% against €STR at 2.19%, generating a +147bp carry advantage for the dollar, matched by central bank policy rates of Fed 3.75% versus ECB 2.4% establishing a +135bp spread. In the derivatives space, EUR/USD ATM IV stands at 7.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, delivering an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.4% as institutional accounts price meaningful protection ahead of central bank events. Leveraged funds hold a net short EUR position of -52,784 contracts at the 31st percentile, reflecting modest short exposure that lacks extreme crowding while headline focus remains on German regional election results. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, capped by carry disadvantage and overhead technical resistance. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Spot clears and closes above the SMA200 at 1.1638, unwinding short-end yield sensitivity.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Technical Cap
signals.text: GBP/USD registers at 1.3508, holding below its downward-sloping 20-day SMA at 1.3555 while remaining above the 50-day SMA at 1.3456 and 200-day SMA at 1.3447. The options complex displays a notable pricing divergence, where 1-month ATM IV at 11.0% stands +6.3 percentage points above 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, signaling heavy hedging activity across market participants. On the policy front, the rate spread sits flat with BoE at 3.75% versus Fed at 3.75% yielding a 0bp nominal differential, while short-term OIS rates show SONIA at 3.73% against SOFR at 3.66% for a marginal -7bp GBP premium. Institutional positioning remains heavily extended at +47,504 leveraged net long contracts in the 93rd percentile, though leveraged funds shed -9,335 contracts WoW as negative economic momentum (-6.7 ESI) compounds topside resistance. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD, technical compression below moving average cluster. Catalyst: UK BRC Retail Sales Monitor at 23:01 UTC. Risk: Spot posts a sustained breakout above the 20-day SMA at 1.3555, prompting options volatility compression.
